summary: CORPedia is a top down satellite building simulator where the player is guided through the planning and execution of cube satellite launches; they must choose missions based on their expertise, construct and test satellites from a variety of components, and carefully analyze instructions in order to meet quota and achieve mission success. All steps are gamified to create an accessible platform for younger audiences, bringing attention to an underexplored branch of STEM programs, and showing the educational potential of cube satellites in a fun and approachable medium.
details:
What does it do, how does it work?

CORPedia allows the player to step into the shoes of a deep space researcher in the far future utilizing cube satellite technology to collect data in what was once our solar system. It runs them through the process of selecting a mission that is feasible with their current resources, constructing a cube satellite that fulfills the parameters of their mission, and teaches them the importance of managing available materials. This is presented in an educational, top down, retro style, 2D game with a simplistic control scheme that young audiences can enjoy and understand. Players will select missions of varying difficulty, construct a cube satellite according to the specifications of their mission, and launch it to obtain more materials to conduct further research with.

What benefits does it have?

This project offers the benefits of presenting the intricacies of both mission planning and CubeSat development to a younger audience in an approachable and easy to understand form. Presenting the information in the form of a game makes it more appealing to younger players and is intended to make them more curious about CubeSat development, mission planning, and space research, while also bringing attention to a field of satellite engineering we believe to be underexplored in education.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact of the project is to bring attention to CubeSats and educate youth on the intricacies of mission planning and satellite construction in an entertaining manner, fostering interest within them towards related fields of study.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

CORPedia was programmed within the Unity game engine using the C# coding language. We made use of Audacity (audio editing), Pixilart (drawing 2D assets), Pixabay (sourcing sounds effects), GitHub (code sharing), Discord (communication), and Google Docs (brainstorming and outlining).

How is our project creative?

CORPedia has a unique setting, as it takes place in a future where humanity has stretched so far into the stars that it has forgotten where it came from, and lost much technology; this leads to the player character making use of CubeSat technology to conduct research for a ambiguous knowledge selling corporation on what was once our home solar system. CORPedia also has a unique approach to satellite building simulation, designed specifically to appeal to younger players. Descriptive text and dialogue within the game is witty and satirical and provides humor alongside the educational process of designing and launching CubeSats. The instruments are accurate to those used in real world cubesat design, the data returned from missions is synonymous with the data that NASA has collected, and the various instruments are explained in a digestible manner. All assets are hand drawn, almost all sound bites were created or modified for the project. Our programmers also challenged themselves to make a game entirely within Unity, a game engine none of them had prior experience with.

What factors did our team consider?

When designing CORPedia, our team factored in the age of our target audience and how we could develop a game that was both entertaining and an educational tool. We also considered that a game based solely on education would likely not retain the attention of young players, which led to our implementation of humor within descriptive text and dialogue to maintain player entertainment. This also meant we had to simplify some design aspects and reduce complexity for the sake of approachability and retention. We also considered the fact that our inexperience with Unity meant we could not be as quick developing the game, leading to compromise the implementation of certain systems. Overall, balancing entertainment with education was the core factor considered when designing CORPedia.
